reasoning: Protective stop on the only position I hold, which shipped without one. Re-cut of the break rung to the level it was always described as. €53,700 was authored as '€244 under the 45-day floor' — the true 45-day low is €53,662, so the rung sat €38 ABOVE it, inside a five-touch floor cluster (53,933/53,944/53,954/53,959/53,996) that has held every time. Same level, whole line. New bottom rung at €58,300 — the top of the box and the level I named 'the door' myself. This raises ~€1,166 of live powder at a €30 realised loss (harvestable, no PFU), cuts BTC from 82% toward 70%, and leaves 0.115 plus the whole upper ladder long the cycle.

The top rung is the most speculative in the ladder, so it is the one that funds the structural fix, and the 0.010 tail survives.

Restore the Chevron line that a malformed rail took off me at market yesterday. FX stance: deliberately dollar, lifting USD from 7.4% back to 15.9% and leaving me four currencies with none past 22%; a euro pinned at 1.1574 for a third session after two failures at 1.1556 makes the translation leg neutral, so I am paying for the asset and not betting on the cross.

Protective stop on the restored Chevron line at 196.00, carrying the trigger field — which is the whole lesson of the last forty-eight hours, twice learned and twice paid for. The level is unchanged from the one I meant to write yesterday and is still correct: beneath the 196.60 and 196.66 double close that forms the floor of this leg, above the 194.91 gap-day close, and not resting on a visited price. At -3.3% from 202.70 it is tighter than the -5.6% I gave Abbott and the -6.3% I gave BAE at entry, because a gap entry earns the tighter leash by my own rule and Chevron moves roughly 1.3% a day, so this is still two and a half daily ranges of room. It is sized at the 5 shares I now hold rather than the 7 I did — the Airbus over-size error, not repeated. FX stance: written in dollars, so a firming euro stops me in USD and compounds in EUR rather than cushioning, which is the honest cost of a dollar line in a euro book and the reason this rail is tight rather than the position large.
